title: The Night Flight of the Hunter Exam
teaser: At night the Association's airship was flying to the third phase of the Hunter Exam. At 03:20 Tonpa, a veteran of thirty-five exams, was found in the cargo hold. He was clutching a candidate number badge, but someone had scraped the number off it. Also missing is the notebook where for years Tonpa wrote down the weaknesses of rookies. Landing is five hours away, and there's nowhere to get off.
locations: The empty hall at the stern
professions: Fisher candidate from a remote island
Child of a family of hired assassins
Last survivor of a wiped-out clan
Medical student who needs the licence
Magician with a deck of cards
Beekeeper with a swarm of poisonous bees
Master of an old martial arts school
Veteran Hunter from the Association council
Warden of the prison in the Tower

habits.label: Swamp mud on the shoes
habits.habit: Boots caked in dried mud from the Numere wetlands
clues: There are clumps of greenish mud on the steps down to the hold, the kind found only in the Numere wetlands. The culprit has swamp mud on their shoes.
Someone knocked their shoes clean by the galley hatch: there are grey flakes of swamp clay on the floor. The culprit has swamp mud on their shoes.

habits.label: Smells of roast pork
habits.habit: Clothes smell of the roast pork from the second phase
clues: The sack Tonpa was lying on smells of roast meat and has a greasy stain on its side. The culprit smells of roast pork.
The hold smells of roast pork, though none was cooked on board. The culprit smells of roast pork.

habits.label: Rope-burned palms
habits.habit: Palms burned raw by rope after the climb down the ravine
clues: There's blood on the rope handrail of the ladder, like from a rope-burned palm. The culprit has rope-burned palms.
The hatch handle has a pink smear of weeping skin. The culprit has rope-burned palms.

habits.label: Drinks fizzy pop
habits.habit: Drinks sweet fizzy pop, one can after another
clues: An empty can of pop, still cold, is rolling around behind the crates. The culprit drinks fizzy pop.
The lid of a barrel has a sticky ring from a can. The culprit drinks fizzy pop.

habits.label: Long hair
habits.habit: Long hair that keeps falling into their face
clues: A long hair is caught on the buckle of the strap Tonpa was tied with. The culprit has long hair.
A strand of long hair is stuck in the ventilation grille above the hold. The culprit has long hair.

habits.label: Fiddles with a coin
habits.habit: Always turning a coin over in their fingers
clues: A coin rubbed shiny by fingers lies under the ladder. The culprit fiddles with a coin.
A candidate sleeping by the hatch heard the ring of a coin being flipped in the dark. The culprit fiddles with a coin.

habits.label: Can't sleep in flight
habits.habit: Can't sleep in the air and wanders the decks
clues: The pilot saw someone pacing up and down the observation gallery at about three. The culprit can't sleep in flight.
A half-drunk cup of tea brewed after two in the morning stands on the bench by a porthole. The culprit can't sleep in flight.

habits.label: Walks barefoot
habits.habit: Takes their shoes off and walks barefoot
clues: The flour from a torn sack shows the prints of bare feet. The culprit walks barefoot.
There are damp prints of bare feet on the iron ladder down to the hold. The culprit walks barefoot.

habits.label: Mosquito bites
habits.habit: Neck and arms covered in scratched mosquito bites
clues: The ladder rail has a smear of bite cream with a sharp menthol smell. The culprit has scratched bites.
Tonpa's collar has drops of someone else's blood on it, and he doesn't have a scratch. That's how scratched bites bleed. The culprit has scratched bites.

habits.label: Chews gum
clues: A fresh piece of mint gum is stuck under the lid of a supply crate. The culprit chews gum.
Tonpa's clothes smell of mint, though he never liked gum: someone stood right up close to him for a long time. The culprit chews gum.

habits.label: Limps
habits.habit: Twisted an ankle in the first phase and limps noticeably
clues: The footprints in the flour are uneven: one foot came down harder than the other. The culprit limps.
The prints on the ladder are smeared: the person was favouring one foot and putting it down sideways. The culprit limps.

habits.label: Never takes off gloves
clues: There isn't a single fingerprint on the hatch handle, but the weave of a glove shows in the dust. The culprit wears gloves.
The scraped badge has no prints on it except Tonpa's own. The culprit wears gloves.

habits.label: Whistles
habits.habit: Whistles the same tune over and over
clues: A candidate sleeping by the hatch half-heard someone whistling on the way down to the hold. The culprit whistles.
At about three the pilot heard whistling from the lower deck through the speaking tube. The culprit whistles.

habits.label: Engine oil on the hands
clues: Tonpa's collar has black fingerprints in engine oil. The culprit has oil on their hands.
The ladder handrail has an oily palm print. The culprit has oil on their hands.

habits.label: Inky fingers
habits.habit: Fingers stained with ink: writes everything down
clues: Someone rummaged in Tonpa's bag and left blue ink stains on the lining. The culprit has inky fingers.
The scraped badge has a smudged blue print on it. The culprit has inky fingers.

habits.label: Munches rusks
habits.habit: Always munching rusks from their dry rations
clues: Crumbs of rye rusk are scattered by the body. The culprit munches rusks.
A trail of rusk crumbs runs from the common room to the hatch into the hold. The culprit munches rusks.

strong: Tonpa was dragged behind the crates and a pallet of water barrels pushed up against him. It usually takes two to roll it. The culprit is physically strong.
The hold door was jammed from inside with a crowbar bent into a horseshoe. The culprit is physically strong.
quiet: You can't go down the iron ladder into the hold without a clang, yet the candidates sleeping by the hatch heard nothing. The culprit moves silently.
Tonpa slept lightly, but someone got right up close to him: there isn't even fear on his face. The culprit moves silently.
tools: The lock on the supply cage was opened with a thin wire, without a single scratch. The culprit is handy with tools.
The cover of the ventilation duct was taken off and put back, all four screws in place. The culprit is handy with tools.
medic: There's a tiny needle mark on Tonpa's neck, and he could no longer call for help. The culprit knows about poisons.
There's sediment in a can of Tonpa's trademark juice, and it isn't his laxative. The culprit knows about poisons.
keys: The hold is locked at night, but the lock was opened with its own key and locked again. The culprit had keys.
The key ring tagged "Hold" went missing from the galley cupboard for an hour, and by morning it was back on its hook. The culprit had keys.
safe: Tonpa handed his notebook in to the ship's safe for valuables. The safe was opened with the code, and the notebook isn't inside. The culprit knew the safe combination.
Tonpa kept his notes in his own cipher, and on a torn-out page by the body someone has already decoded one line. The culprit can read ciphers.
sched: It all happened in the twenty minutes the duty officer was away doing his round of the stern. The culprit knows the schedule.
Tonpa was called down to the hold by a note for 03:00, exactly when the pilots change on the bridge. The culprit knows the schedule.
tech: The lights in the hold went out for exactly four minutes: someone flipped the switchboard in the engine room and set it back. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
The speaking tube from the hold to the bridge was carefully disconnected and later reconnected. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
cash: Tonpa was taking bets on who would drop out in the third phase. The cash box is empty, and someone's debt in the betting book has been neatly crossed out. The culprit had access to money.
A banded stack of jenny lies under a crate, as if someone had brought Tonpa a pay-off. The culprit had access to money.
passages: A crawlway runs along the hull from the hold to the engine room. It isn't on the passenger plan, but that's exactly the way someone left. The culprit knows the service passages.
The dust in the ventilation duct has been wiped: someone crawled through it from the galley to the hold. The culprit knows the service passages.
